action_en: Avoid formulating mandarin fish feeds with high carbohydrate or high fat levels, and keep carbohydrate below the range where feed intake fell (above about 16.5%).
action_zh: 饲料企业应避免为鳜鱼配制高碳水化合物或高脂肪饲料,并将碳水化合物含量控制在摄食量开始下降的范围(约16.5%以上)之下。
evidence_gap: The best carbohydrate-to-lipid ratio is not specified, and one study reported anorexia at 8% carbohydrate, so the safe threshold is unclear.
risks: Lowering carbohydrate may raise feed cost through more protein or lipid, and high-fat diets also caused liver damage.

basis.reason: F0563, F0535 and F0546 all link high carbohydrate or high fat to reduced feeding, liver damage, oxidative stress and weaker immunity in mandarin fish, and F0115 supports a balanced carbohydrate-to-lipid ratio for appetite. I left out F0577 and F0578 because they disagree or only describe diets. The type is avoid for clearly high levels, but I gave no exact target since F0115 gives no ratio and F0563 contains a conflicting 8% result.

findings.why: Feed intake fell between 16.5% and 30.1% carbohydrate, with poorer growth at the highest levels.
High carbohydrate linked to oxidative stress, liver apoptosis, intestinal damage and lower immunity.
High-fat diets caused liver damage and steatosis.
An appropriate carbohydrate-to-lipid ratio supported appetite, but no ratio was given.

priority.reason: Measured, largely agreeing evidence from many papers (32 and 22 claims) links high carbohydrate and high fat to lower feed intake, liver and gut damage, and oxidative stress. Feed makers can act on it now, and the 16.5% carbohydrate figure gives a usable limit even though the 8% anorexia report leaves the safe threshold unclear.

criteria.note: Anorexia and liver damage across fed fish

action_en: Monitor total ammonia nitrogen and nitrite regularly in mandarin fish tanks and keep ammonia low, since the fish tolerate it poorly.
action_zh: 养殖者应定期监测鳜养殖水体的总氨氮和亚硝酸盐,并将氨氮保持在低水平,因为鳜对氨耐受性较差。
evidence_gap: No study measures whether monitoring improves welfare, and the safe long-term ammonia level is unclear because one other study found no deaths or added gill damage.
risks: Testing costs time and equipment, and the limits reported (ammonia below 0.2–0.5 mg/L, nitrite below 0.05 mg/L) come from rearing trials rather than from tests of welfare thresholds.

basis.reason: F0457 shows ammonia harmed juveniles (LC50 12.91 mg/L, liver stress, and lower gill enzyme activity at one time point), and F0527 states that tolerance is low so strict control is needed. F0528 supplies the monitoring practice and limits used in culture. Because the effect of monitoring itself is not measured and one study found milder effects, I kept this at monitor and not adopt.

findings.why: Shows ammonia caused mortality and chronic liver and gill effects, with one conflicting study.
Reports low ammonia tolerance and the ranges commonly held in trials.
Describes monitoring intervals and the ammonia and nitrite limits used.

priority.reason: Ammonia harm is well measured (114 claims, 92 measured, LC50 12.91 mg/L, chronic liver and gill effects), and testing is cheap for any farm. Most of the evidence comes from one main study, and one other study found no deaths, so the safe level is not firm.

criteria.note: Death and chronic organ stress, all farms
Large but dominated by one study

action_en: Avoid holding mandarin fish at water temperatures up to 36°C, and treat temperatures at that level as a welfare risk to be corrected.
action_zh: 养殖者应避免将鳜养殖水温长期保持在高达36°C的水平,并将此类温度视为需要纠正的福利风险。
evidence_gap: The studies tested 36°C in controlled trials, so the temperature at which harm begins between about 30°C and 36°C on commercial farms is not defined.
risks: Cooling or shading to prevent such temperatures adds energy and equipment costs, and the findings do not say what level is a safe upper limit.

basis.reason: Both findings report harm at 36°C: strongly inhibited growth, lower liver antioxidant enzymes, higher liver oxidative damage, and signs of immune fatigue in females. I chose these over the feeding findings because they show a direct harm at high temperature. The harm comes from trials at one extreme temperature, so I limited the action to avoiding that range and did not set a recommended temperature.

findings.why: Growth inhibition and antioxidant and heat-shock changes at 36°C, read as exceeding the fish's self-protection range.
Higher liver oxidative damage and immune fatigue in females at up to 36°C.

priority.reason: Seven papers with 18 measured claims show 36°C inhibits growth and weakens antioxidant defences. Avoiding it is a clear step, but the harm threshold between 30°C and 36°C is undefined and cooling costs money.

criteria.note: Heat stress where summer peaks occur
Shading or water exchange, some cost

action_en: Avoid training mandarin fish onto compound feed by direct starvation, and watch trained groups for emaciation and fish that stop eating.
action_zh: 养殖户应避免用直接饥饿法驯食让鳜鱼摄食配合饲料,并密切观察驯食组是否出现消瘦和拒食。
evidence_gap: No trial compares starvation training with gradual methods using the same fish, feed and conditions, and the measured welfare outcomes come from very few studies.
risks: Dropping starvation training may lengthen the training period and raise bait fish use in the short term, and gradual methods have their own failures.

basis.reason: All three findings report poor outcomes when mandarin fish are forced onto artificial feed: zero domestication rate, regurgitation and deaths, 53% emaciated fish in one trial, and anorexia-related gene expression in fish that resisted training. I left out the findings on successful stepwise domestication because they cover a different method. The type is avoid rather than a stronger action because only two measured trials address starvation directly, and F0121 and F0207 are mixed.

findings.why: Two trials where starvation training gave no or late feeding, regurgitation, deaths and a zero domestication rate.
findings.practice_en: starvation direct training to compound feed

findings.why: Measured trial with 53% emaciated trained fish versus 6% of controls.
Fish hard to domesticate had higher anorexia-related gene expression and low survival.

priority.reason: Two measured studies found direct starvation training failed (zero domestication, deaths, regurgitation), and a trial found 53% emaciation in trained fish. The step is cheap, but there are few papers and no head-to-head comparison with gradual methods.

criteria.note: Starvation, death, emaciation in trained fish

action_en: Trial stepwise domestication from live bait to dead fish and then formulated feed, with a probiotic added to the pellets, on commercial farms, tracking acceptance, survival and emaciation.
action_zh: 养殖户应在商业养殖场试验从活饵到死鱼再到配合饲料的逐步驯食,并在饲料中添加益生菌,同时记录摄食率、成活率和消瘦情况。
evidence_gap: It is unknown which stepwise schedule and probiotic combination works best on farms, and whether stress or injury is lower than with other methods.
risks: Fish that accept feed only partly may grow unevenly and lose weight, and probiotic effects were tested in one study with only inferred links to appetite.

basis.reason: F0567 and F0561 describe the gradual transition and acceptance rates, while F0550 and F0581 add probiotics as a possible aid for appetite and gut health in pellet-fed fish. I did not cite F0559 because its claims on artificial feed replacing live bait are mixed and the others already cover its useful points. The type is test_on_farms because acceptance is partial, no welfare outcomes were measured, and the probiotic evidence rests on few measured studies.

findings.why: Stepwise domestication reached roughly 70-88% acceptance but only some individuals accepted feed and no welfare measures were taken.
findings.practice_en: feeding domestication of mandarin fish to formulated feed
findings.practice_zh: 鳜鱼驯食（条件反射驯化）

findings.why: Describes mixed live and artificial feed transition schedules.
findings.practice_en: feed transition from live/fresh feed to artificial feed
findings.practice_zh: 饵料驯化(鲜活饵料向人工配合饲料过渡)

findings.why: Probiotics restored immune markers, appetite genes and gut structure in pellet-fed fish over 28 days.
One study inferred that probiotics raised appetite in pellet-fed fish.

priority.reason: Stepwise domestication has the broadest support (9 papers, 17 claims, 9 measured), with acceptance of 70-100% depending on feed type. None of it measures welfare outcomes, and the probiotic link is only inferred, so a farm trial is the right step.

criteria.note: Reduces live bait dependence and starvation

action_en: Test dietary betaine in high-carbohydrate or high-fat mandarin fish diets on farms, measuring feed intake, liver condition and growth.
action_zh: 饲料企业和养殖户应在养殖场试验在高碳水或高脂鳜鱼饲料中添加甜菜碱,并测定摄食量、肝脏状况和生长。
evidence_gap: Effects were shown in controlled trials on specific diets, with no farm-scale data on dose, long-term welfare or disease resistance.
risks: One paper found no significant difference in feeding rates, and betaine may only offset harm from diets that are already poorly balanced.

basis.reason: Both findings concern betaine in mandarin fish on high-carbohydrate diets, with measured gains in appetite-related genes and feed intake (F0155) and reduced liver stress and lipid deposition (F0045). I picked them over the taurine and tributyrin findings, which are mostly background or not tested in this species. The type is test_on_farms because the evidence agrees but comes from few controlled trials and does not address infectious disease.

findings.why: Betaine raised feed intake and appetite genes, though one paper found no difference in feeding rates.
Betaine reduced liver oxidative stress, ER stress, apoptosis and lipid deposition on high-carbohydrate diets.

priority.reason: Betaine measurably raised feed intake and cut liver stress in 3 papers with high-carbohydrate or high-fat diets, but one paper found no feeding difference. It may only offset badly balanced diets, and there is no farm-scale or dose data.

criteria.note: Appetite and liver stress under poor diets
Measured but few papers, lab only

action_en: Run farm trials of the licensed inactivated ISKNV vaccine and the bivalent ISKNV-SCRV vaccine in mandarin fish, recording disease losses and the conditions of use, before recommending wider adoption.
action_zh: 在养殖场开展鳜鱼灭活ISKNV疫苗和ISKNV-SCRV二价疫苗的试验，记录发病损失和使用条件，再考虑推广。
evidence_gap: Protection figures are mostly background statements without test conditions, and general vaccination claims give no welfare data or conditions under which it works.
risks: Injection requires handling and anesthesia, which may stress fish, and vaccine cost and labour fall on the farm.

basis.reason: F0316 gives the most specific protection figures (90% for a licensed vaccine) and F0348 supports vaccination more generally, so they fit together as one vaccine action. Both agree, but the figures are mostly background and lack test conditions, and F0348 has no measured data, so I chose farm trials rather than adoption. I left out the preparation findings because they report no effect.

findings.why: reports ISKNV protection above 80-90% for inactivated vaccines
general support for vaccination against viral and bacterial disease, but no data

priority.reason: Viral disease is severe and widespread, and a licensed ISKNV vaccine is reported at 90% protection. Most of the figures are background statements with no conditions, so farm trials are warranted before recommending adoption. Injection stress is a cost.

action_en: Monitor dissolved oxygen continuously in dense mandarin fish culture and keep it at or above about 5.5 mg/L to avoid hypoxia, which may raise viral outbreak risk.
action_zh: 养殖者应在高密度鳜养殖中持续监测溶解氧,并将其保持在约5.5 mg/L以上以避免缺氧,缺氧可能增加病毒暴发风险。
evidence_gap: The link between hypoxia and disease in mandarin fish rests on background statements and no study measured disease outcomes at defined oxygen levels or densities.
risks: Extra aeration costs energy and cannot by itself be shown to prevent disease, and oxygen swings from hypoxia to supersaturation can occur in intensive systems.

basis.reason: F0601 and F0406 say hypoxia is common in intensive farming and may promote ISKNV replication, while F0484 and F0527 give oxygen levels kept in trials and note that fish surface when oxygen is short. F0394 shows continuous aeration is the usual way oxygen is kept up but reports no disease effect. Since the disease link is only background and no measured benefit exists, the action is monitoring and not a firm adoption.

findings.why: Describes unstable oxygen and hypoxia in intensive farming, linked to disease outbreaks.
Background says hypoxia can promote ISKNV replication; measured claims show physiological stress under hypoxia.
Gives the practice of keeping dissolved oxygen at 5.5 mg/L or more.
Reports oxygen of about 5 mg/L or higher is held and that fish surface when oxygen is short.
Shows continuous aeration keeps oxygen at 7.0–9.3 mg/L but gives no disease result.

priority.reason: Keeping dissolved oxygen at or above 5.5 mg/L is cheap and plausible, and hypoxia stress is measured. The link to viral outbreaks rests on background statements, and the DO findings only describe practice.

action_en: Test on trial ponds or tanks how water temperature in the 19–30°C range trades off virus risk (ISKNV, MRV) against feeding and growth in mandarin fish.
action_zh: 研究人员应在试验池或养殖缸中检验19–30°C范围内的水温如何在病毒(ISKNV、MRV)风险与鳜摄食和生长之间权衡。
evidence_gap: No study has compared disease outcomes and feeding or growth across the same set of temperatures in one trial, and feed intake results conflict between trials.
risks: Challenge trials with ISKNV or MRV could cause fish deaths and need strict biosecurity, and results from lab trials may not carry over to farms.

basis.reason: F0602 shows ISKNV caused no disease at about 19–20°C but was highly lethal above 20°C, and MRV deaths rose at 26°C. F0607 and F0606 show feeding activity and feed efficiency are higher at about 26–31°C than at 20–23°C, so the two aims point to different temperatures. Because the findings are mixed and come from separate studies, I propose research rather than recommending a temperature.

findings.why: Virus disease outcome depends on temperature, with a threshold near 20°C for ISKNV.
Feeding starts above about 15°C and is higher at about 26–30°C, but intake results are inconsistent.
Weight gain and feed efficiency were higher at 26–31°C than at 20°C, while intake did not follow the same pattern.

priority.reason: Temperature strongly governs virus outcomes (no disease at 19-20°C, deaths above) and feeding, so the stake is large. Feed intake results conflict and no trial covers disease and growth together, so this research fills the main evidence gap.

action_en: Use PCR or LAMP pathogen testing on mandarin fish with signs of disease to confirm the pathogen, such as ISKNV, Aeromonas hydrophila, Nocardia or ranavirus, before choosing a treatment.
action_zh: 对出现病症的鳜鱼采用PCR或LAMP检测确认病原（如ISKNV、嗜水气单胞菌、诺卡氏菌、蛙病毒），再选择治疗方案。
evidence_gap: The claims measure detection performance only, and no study shows that testing improves fish welfare or disease outcomes.
risks: Testing costs time and money, and a duplex LAMP test covers only two pathogens, so other agents may be missed.

basis.reason: Both findings agree that these tests identify disease agents in mandarin fish, and F0589 notes that early frog virus disease looks like bacterial disease, so testing allows a rational treatment choice. I put them together because they serve the same diagnostic purpose; LAMP adds a simple on-site option. They show detection ability, not welfare gains, so the action is limited to confirming pathogens before treatment.

findings.why: PCR, sequencing and histopathology identify or rule out agents; early viral and bacterial disease look alike
duplex LAMP-HNB detects A. hydrophila and ISKNV at 100 fg with simple equipment
findings.practice_zh: LAMP环介导等温扩增病原检测

priority.reason: PCR and LAMP testing are measured to detect pathogens well, allowing treatment to be matched to the cause. No study shows better fish welfare outcomes, and cost and coverage limits apply.

action_en: Base antibiotic choice for bacterial disease in mandarin fish on susceptibility testing of the farm's own isolates, treat early, and monitor for resistance.
action_zh: 鳜鱼细菌性疾病的抗生素选择应基于本场分离菌株的药敏试验，尽早治疗，并监测耐药性。
evidence_gap: The claims report only in-vitro sensitivity and recommended regimens, not treatment effects on fish health, and the two studies differ on some drugs.
risks: Antibiotic use can drive resistance, and sensitivity in one strain may not predict results on another farm.

basis.reason: F0346 shows that sensitivity differs between strains and between studies, and F0587 recommends susceptibility-guided, early treatment with resistance monitoring, so they combine into a testing-first approach. F0346 is mixed and neither finding measures fish outcomes, so I framed this as monitoring and susceptibility checks rather than endorsing specific drugs.

findings.why: strains show both sensitivity and resistance, and studies differ on some drugs
supports early, susceptibility-guided treatment and resistance monitoring
findings.practice_zh: 抗生素治疗细菌性疾病

priority.reason: Susceptibility-guided antibiotic use is sensible, but the evidence is only in-vitro sensitivity from two papers that disagree on some drugs. No treatment outcomes were measured, and resistance is a risk.

action_en: Run controlled research trials comparing MS-222, eugenol, 2-phenoxyethanol, clove oil and percussive head-blow stunning in mandarin fish, measuring stress, time to loss of consciousness, recovery and handling or transport outcomes.
action_zh: 研究人员应开展对照试验，比较MS-222、丁香酚、2-苯氧乙醇、丁香油和头部重击击晕对鳜鱼的效果，测量应激、失去意识时间、恢复情况以及操作和运输结果。
evidence_gap: No cited claim measures how any anesthetic or physical stunning method affects mandarin fish welfare during handling, transport or slaughter, and the doses used vary widely (about 20 to 200 mg/L for MS-222).
risks: Trials impose handling and anesthetic exposure on fish and cost research effort, and results from sampling doses may not transfer to farm slaughter or transport conditions.

basis.reason: All three findings only describe anesthesia or physical stunning being used in mandarin fish, and none report a measured welfare effect, so they point to the same gap and belong together. I did not pick any method as better because the findings give no comparison. The evidence is only descriptive, so the action is research rather than adoption.

findings.why: MS-222 used at about 20-200 mg/L for sampling, with no welfare outcome measured
Head-blow stunning described and labelled humane, but no measured welfare effect
Eugenol, 2-phenoxyethanol and clove oil described for sampling, with no measured welfare effect

priority.reason: Slaughter and handling welfare is potentially large, and the evidence gap is clear: 33 papers only describe MS-222 use and none measure welfare effects. The gain for mandarin fish is not shown, so a research action sits mid-low.

criteria.note: Slaughter and handling for all fish
Trial burden on fish is limited

action_en: Test salt water bath disinfection and quarantine with PCR screening before stocking mandarin fish, measuring disease and parasite outcomes and any stress or injury to the fish.
action_zh: 在鳜鱼放养前试验盐水浴消毒及检疫加PCR筛查，并测量发病、寄生虫情况以及对鱼的应激或损伤。
evidence_gap: No claim reports measured disease or parasite outcomes for salt baths or quarantine, and the effective salt concentrations and durations are not compared.
risks: A 3%-5% salt bath is a strong stressor and could harm fish if exposure is too long, and quarantine adds holding time and cost.

basis.reason: Both describe pre-stocking biosecurity steps meant to keep pathogens out, so they fit one trial. Both only describe the practice and none reports outcomes or negative effects, so I chose testing rather than adoption.

findings.why: salt bath (3%-5%, 5-10 min) or iodine described as killing surface pathogens, no outcomes
findings.practice_en: salt water bath disinfection before stocking

findings.why: quarantine of 1-2+ weeks with PCR confirmation of freedom from MRV or ISKNV, no outcomes

priority.reason: Salt baths and quarantine are plausible biosecurity steps, but the claims only describe the practice with no measured disease outcomes. A 3-5% salt bath is itself a stressor.

action_en: Screen live bait fish for pathogens and parasites before feeding them to mandarin fish, and record disease events on farms that use live bait or farm at high density.
action_zh: 兽医应在以活饵投喂鳜鱼前检测活饵鱼的病原体和寄生虫,并记录使用活饵或高密度养殖的养殖场的疾病发生情况。
evidence_gap: The claims are background statements with no measured infection rates or conditions, and artificial feed did not clearly lower disease risk in measured results.
risks: Screening adds cost and may miss pathogens, and the findings do not show it prevents outbreaks.

basis.reason: F0056 says live bait can introduce pathogens and parasites, and F0071 links intensive farming to viral disease and the parasite Anchitrema sinense, so both point to watching for disease. I included F0537 because its measured results show artificial feed is not a clear disease-reducing alternative. The type is monitor rather than avoid because the claims are background statements with no measured effects.

findings.why: Background claims that live bait can bring in pathogens or parasites and cause mass mortality.
High-density farming is linked to viral disease and parasite infection, mostly from background statements.
Measured results show artificial feed linked to liver damage and weaker immunity, so replacing live bait is not a clear fix.
findings.practice_zh: 人工饲料替代活饵养殖

priority.reason: Live bait carrying pathogens and high-density disease links are background statements with no measured infection rates. Screening has unproven benefit and adds cost, though recording disease events is cheap.

criteria.note: Zero measured claims on bait risk

action_en: Test on commercial mandarin fish farms whether qPCR screening of spleen, liver and kidney tissue can detect chronic viral infection earlier than conventional PCR, and whether earlier detection leads to better disease handling.
action_zh: 在商业鳜鱼养殖场开展试验，检验对脾、肝、肾组织进行qPCR筛查是否比常规PCR更早发现慢性病毒感染，以及早期发现是否有助于改善疾病处理。
evidence_gap: The findings show qPCR detects very low viral DNA in lab studies, but not whether using it on farms improves fish health or welfare outcomes.
risks: Organ sampling needs dead or sacrificed fish, and testing adds cost and lab work; a positive result may not mean the fish are suffering.

basis.reason: Only F0359 concerns disease detection, so the action rests on it alone. It is rated only 'described': the four claims show qPCR is sensitive (it found viral DNA that conventional PCR missed, and MFBV in dead fish but not controls) but give no welfare effect. That is why this is a farm trial rather than adoption.

findings.why: Shows qPCR found low-level viral DNA that conventional PCR missed, and MFBV in dead fish; no welfare outcome reported.

priority.reason: qPCR is measured to detect low viral loads, but there is no evidence that farm use improves fish health. Organ sampling needs sacrificed fish, and a positive result does not show suffering.

action_en: Study whether probiotic supplementation reduces disease in mandarin fish, since current claims are general statements rather than results in this species.
action_zh: 研究益生菌添加是否能降低鳜鱼疾病发生，因为目前的说法只是一般性陈述，并非该物种的试验结果。
evidence_gap: No measured effect of probiotics on disease in mandarin fish, nor the conditions or strains involved, is reported.
risks: Probiotics may fail to match antibiotic or vaccine protection, and relying on them could delay effective disease control.

basis.reason: F0591 is the only finding on probiotics, and it agrees that they are a promising alternative to antibiotics. Both claims are general and none was measured in this species, so only research is supported.

findings.why: general claims of antibacterial use and antibiotic substitution, with no measured effect in mandarin fish

priority.reason: Probiotic disease claims are general statements with no measured effect in mandarin fish, so research is justified. The disease gain at stake is unproven and the evidence gap is not the only barrier.

action_en: Test in live mandarin fish whether potassium permanganate, iodophor or probiotics added to the water reduce disease, and check their safety for the fish.
action_zh: 研究人员应在活体鳜中检验向水体添加高锰酸钾、碘伏或益生菌能否减少疾病,并检查其对鱼的安全性。
evidence_gap: The only measured effects are virus titre reductions in the lab and unmeasured claims of better immunity, with no data on disease or survival in fish.
risks: Disinfectants at the concentrations that cut virus titre (2000 ppm and above) may be harmful to fish, and probiotics may have no effect on disease.

basis.reason: These three findings all concern adding agents to water against disease, and each shows only an indirect signal: virus titre falls of 4–8 log units, or claimed immune and water quality benefits. None measures disease in fish, and the doses in hatching tanks (20 mg/L and 30 mg/L) differ from the high doses used for virus kill. That is why the action is research and not adoption.

findings.why: Potassium permanganate lowered virus titre by 5–8 log units, and 20 mg/L was used on hatching tanks.
Iodophor lowered virus titre by 4–8 log units, and 30 mg/L povidone-iodine was used in tanks after hatching.
Probiotics in water are claimed to improve water quality and immunity, without disease outcomes.

priority.reason: Water additives are supported only by lab virus titre drops at high doses (2000 ppm and above) and unmeasured immunity claims. No disease or survival data exist, and the doses may harm fish.

criteria.note: Lab titre only, no fish outcomes

action_en: Research whether feed intake measured by counting remaining feeder fish or weighing siphoned uneaten feed can serve as a welfare indicator in mandarin fish.
action_zh: 研究通过清点剩余饵料鱼数量或称量虹吸出的残饵重量来测定摄食量，能否作为鳜鱼福利指标。
evidence_gap: No finding links these feed intake measures to any welfare outcome, so it is unknown whether they reflect fish welfare.
risks: Counting feeder fish or siphoning uneaten feed means handling and disturbance, and intake alone may mislead about welfare.

basis.reason: F0366 only describes two ways intake was measured (feeder fish number difference and uneaten feed weight). Both papers agree on the method, but neither reports a welfare effect, so no adoption or testing recommendation is supported. Research is the only type the evidence allows.

findings.why: Describes the two intake measurement methods (C1688, C2445); no welfare outcome reported.
findings.practice_en: feed intake assessment by quantity difference
findings.practice_zh: 基于数量差的摄食量评估

priority.reason: The claims only describe how feed intake was measured, with no link to welfare. Intake alone may mislead, and the welfare gain is small and indirect.
